topic: What are the implications of operating across 20-40 GHz on frequency planning for adjacent beams given the increased number of active elements in the FPA?
consensus_response: The increased number of active elements in the Field-Programmable Array (FPA) at 20-40 GHz leads to increased interference between adjacent beams, reducing capacity due to co-channel interference. Narrower beams in higher frequency bands limit the effective spread of rays, changing selectivity properties of the equivalent channel. This affects system parameters such as beamforming and scheduling granularity. True Time Delay (TDD) implemented in optical ICS can alleviate frequency-dependent delays, but may require additional calibration and complexity.
reference_context: Operating across 20-40 GHz increases interference between adjacent beams due to tighter spacing required at higher frequencies, affecting capacity and system parameters such as beamforming and scheduling granularity. True Time Delay (TDD) in optical ICS can alleviate frequency-dependent delays.
